docs.title: Wolds Record help
docs.text: Guides for organisations and practitioners using Wolds Record to keep client, dog and treatment records.

docs.title: New to Wolds Record?
docs.text:
Follow these steps in order:

  1. Sign in and create your account
  2. Create or join your organisation
  3. Set up your account
  4. Create your first client and dog
  5. Open a case and record your first session

docs.title: Guides
docs.text:
Clients and dogsAdd clients and dogs, and set up a treatment record.

CasesOpen, update and close treatment cases.

SessionsRecord treatment sessions.

Vet reportsGenerate and share reports for vets.

Calendar (beta)Appointments, booking requests and payments.

Organisation settingsPractice details, billing and data export.

docs.title: Get in touch
docs.text:
• Open the app: https://app.woldsrecord.com/dashboard
  • Marketing website: https://www.woldsrecord.com/
  • Support: support@woldsrecord.com

Wolds Record is operated by Benjamin Whitfield-Heap, trading as Wolds Record.

docs.title: Create your organisation
docs.text:
After first sign-in, if no active organisation exists, you are directed to onboarding.

  1. Enter your organisation details.
  2. Submit the onboarding form.
  3. You are added as the initial organisation member.
  4. The new organisation becomes your active organisation.

docs.title: Switch active organisation
docs.text:
If you are a member of multiple organisations, use the organisation switcher to make one organisation active.

Your active organisation controls which clients, dogs, cases, sessions, and settings you can access.

docs.title: Access and permissions
docs.text: If you try to open an organisation where you are not a member, access is blocked and you are redirected.

docs.title: Create an account
docs.text:
1. Open the sign-in screen.
  2. Leave the mode set to Create your account.
  3. Enter your Email address and Password.
  4. Select Create account.
  5. Complete the bot protection check if prompted.
  6. Open the verification email and confirm the account before signing in.

docs.title: Sign in with an existing account
docs.text:
1. On the sign-in screen, select Use existing account.
  2. Enter your email and password.
  3. Complete the bot protection check if prompted.
  4. Select Sign in.

After success, you are redirected to your dashboard.

docs.title: Sign out
docs.text: Use Sign Out in the top navigation. This ends your current session and returns you to the sign-in page.

docs.title: Common issues
docs.text:
• Invalid login credentials: re-check email/password and try again.
  • No confirmation email: check junk/spam and retry sign-up.
  • Email not verified: open the latest verification email, complete confirmation, then sign in again.
  • Session lost: sign in again from /sign-in.

docs.title: Product Overview
docs.text:
Wolds Record, operated by Benjamin Whitfield-Heap trading as Wolds Record, supports canine rehabilitation practitioners with structured, searchable case records.

This section will grow to include end-user workflows and screen-level guidance.

docs.title: Calendar (beta)
docs.text:
Calendar provides online booking, diary scheduling and appointment requests for canine rehabilitation practices.

Beta

Calendar is currently in beta. Owners and admins can turn beta access on or off in Organisation settings.

docs.title: Calendar navigation
docs.text:
When beta access is enabled, the main navigation includes Calendar (/booking), structured into three tabs:

  • Schedule: your calendar diary and list of appointments.
  • Requests: client booking requests awaiting practitioner review.
  • Settings: booking page configuration, services, working hours, booking rules, and payments.

docs.title: Schedule and diary
docs.text: The Schedule tab displays your appointments and diary availability.

docs.title: Calendar views
docs.text:
Switch views using the view buttons in the calendar header:

  • Week: 7-day view of appointments and availability blocks.
  • Day: single-day detailed schedule.
  • Agenda: chronological list of upcoming appointments.

Use Previous, Today and Next to navigate dates.

docs.title: Block time in your diary
docs.text:
Practitioners can block time in their diary with a note (for example, lunch, cleaning, or personal time). Public booking, client reschedules and approved moves will not offer that time.

  1. Select Block time from the calendar header (or click an empty slot and choose Block time).
  2. Enter the Date, Start time and End time.
  3. Enter a Note (for example, "Lunch"). Your colleagues can see this note, but health details should not be included.
  4. Select Save.

To edit or remove a block, select the blocked slot on the calendar, update the details or choose Remove block.

docs.title: Appointment details
docs.text: Selecting an appointment opens a drawer with appointment details, linked client and dog information, and payment status.

docs.title: Booking requests
docs.text:
When dog owners request an appointment through your public booking page, their request appears under Requests. Pending requests also appear in the header Notifications tray, and selecting one opens it for review.

Requests has two tabs, which filter both the list and the calendar:

  • Pending: requests waiting for you to confirm or decline.
  • Reviewed: requests you have confirmed or declined. A reviewed request shows its appointment's payment status.

On a phone, each request is a compact row that opens in a sheet.

docs.title: Review a booking request
docs.text:
1. Open Requests from the Calendar tabs, or select the request in the Notifications tray.
  2. Select a request to open the review panel.
  3. Review the requested service, date, time and owner details.
  4. Link the request to an existing record, or allow the system to create the client and dog:
    • Search existing: enter the client or dog name in Search client or dog and select the match. If the owner's email matches an existing client, the request opens already linked to that client, marked Matched by email. If several clients share the email, you choose between them.
    • New client and dog: check the details prefilled from the owner's request.
  5. If payment is enabled, decide whether to request online payment when confirming.
  6. Select Confirm and book to accept the request, or Decline request if you cannot accommodate it. Before declining, you are asked to confirm, with the dog's name and requested time shown.

docs.title: Expired requests
docs.text: If the requested time passes before you review a request, the request is marked Expired and leaves the Pending tab. The dog owner is not emailed. If the request was to move an existing appointment, that appointment stays as it was.

docs.title: Correct an owner's email address
docs.text:
If an owner entered a wrong email address during booking:

  1. Open the request or appointment review panel.
  2. Update the email under Email.
  3. Save the change. The old management links are invalidated, and booking confirmation emails are resent to the corrected address.

docs.title: Calendar settings
docs.text: Configure your booking experience under Settings in Calendar:

docs.title: Booking page
docs.text:
Configure your public booking page under Settings → Booking page:

  • Booking page state: choose On (dog owners can request appointments), Paused (shows your paused message instead of the form), or Off.
  • Booking page address: customise your organisation's booking link slug.
  • QR code: download a QR code PNG for print materials or client sharing.
  • Preview: select Preview booking page to test the booking flow as dog owners see it.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Define the services clients can book under Settings → Services:

  1. Select Add service.
  2. Enter the Name and optional Description.
  3. Set Duration (minutes).
  4. Set optional Price (£).
  5. Set Buffer time after appointment (in minutes) for notes, cleaning or travel between appointments.
  6. Select Save service.

docs.title: Hours & time off
docs.text:
Set your regular working hours and availability exceptions under Settings → Hours & time off:

  • Weekly hours: set start and end times for each day of the week you accept bookings.
  • Time off & exceptions: add specific dates where hours differ or where you are unavailable (e.g. holidays).

docs.title: Booking rules
docs.text:
Control booking constraints under Settings → Booking rules:

  • Minimum notice: how many hours in advance an owner must book (e.g. 24 hours).
  • Booking window: how far into the future appointments can be scheduled (e.g. 60 days).
  • Slot interval: the spacing of start times offered to clients (e.g. every 15 or 30 minutes).
  • Self-cancel cut-off: the cut-off time before an appointment after which owners can no longer cancel online and must contact the practice directly.
  • Cancellation policy: terms shown to owners before they submit a booking request.

docs.title: Payments
docs.text:
Test mode

Client payments through Stripe Connect are in test mode and currently limited to test organisations during the beta.

Under Settings → Payments, practice owners and admins can connect a Stripe account to take payments for bookings:

  • Connect a Stripe account via Stripe-hosted onboarding.
  • Choose whether priced services require online payment when requests are accepted.
  • Track payment statuses across appointments: Payment due, Payment processing, Paid, Not required, Refund due, and Refunded. Payment processing shows while a delayed payment method, such as Bacs Direct Debit, clears.

docs.title: Create and manage clients and dogs
Create a client
docs.text:
From Clients:

  1. Select New client.
  2. Enter:
    • Client name (required)
    • Email (optional)
    • Phone (optional)
    • Address (optional)
  3. Select Create client.

docs.title: Add a dog to a client
docs.text:
From the client record:

  1. Select Add dog.
  2. Enter the Dog name (required). Sex, age, ownership duration and neutered status are optional and can be left as unknown.
  3. Optionally set breed and vet practice.
  4. Select Create dog.

docs.title: Vet practice assignment during dog setup
docs.text:
When adding a dog, you can:

  • Select an existing vet practice, or
  • Create a new practice inline and assign it immediately.

docs.title: Dog record
docs.text:
A dog's record is the hub for the dog's current treatment record. It has four tabs:

  • Overview: the setup checklist while the treatment record is being set up. Once setup is complete, it shows recent sessions and the consent status.
  • Sessions: the sessions in the current treatment record.
  • Forms: owner consent and the veterinary declaration, with completed forms, and the practice information and terms shown to the owner.
  • Details: treatment details, external resources, the dog summary and previous treatment records.

docs.title: Set up a treatment record
docs.text:
Until a new treatment record is set up, the Overview tab shows Set up this treatment record. Every new treatment record needs owner consent and a vet declaration before the first session. The steps are:

  1. Owner consent
  2. Veterinary declaration
  3. Treatment details (optional)
  4. First session

Each step links to where you complete it. When every step is done, the checklist is replaced by Setup complete.

docs.title: Record consent you already hold
docs.text:
If you received owner consent or a vet declaration outside Wolds Record, for example on a signed paper form, record it on the treatment record:

  1. Open the dog's record.
  2. On the Overview or Forms tab, find Owner consent or Veterinary declaration and select Record existing.
  3. Enter the Date received and, optionally, Notes.
  4. Select Save consent or Save declaration.

To change a recorded entry, select Update. If it was recorded in error, select Clear manual entry or Clear recorded status. Its history is kept.

If a vet declaration is not needed, select Not needed and record your reason.

docs.title: Collect consent with an online form
docs.text:
Wolds Record does not send form links. You copy the link and send it yourself.

  1. Open the dog's record.
  2. On the Overview or Forms tab, select Use online form next to Owner consent or Veterinary declaration.
  3. A locked preview shows the form as the owner or vet practice will see it. Check it, then select Create link.
  4. Select Copy link and send it to the owner or vet practice.

To stop a link working, select Deactivate link. Recorded consent and completed online forms stay on file.

docs.title: View a completed form
docs.text: When an owner or vet practice has completed an online form, select View completed form next to it. The vet declaration shows the wording as it was signed.

docs.title: Edit a dog
docs.text:
1. Open the dog's record.
  2. On the Details tab, open the actions menu on the Dog summary card and select Edit Dog.
  3. Update the details. Only Dog name is required. Sex and Neutered can be set to Unknown, and age can be left blank.
  4. Select Save changes.

docs.title: "No active organisation"
docs.text: Your account is not currently set to an active organisation. Re-run onboarding or switch organisation.

docs.title: "Access denied" / redirected to unauthorized
docs.text: Your user is not a member of that organisation or does not have access to that route.

docs.title: "Missing ... details"
docs.text: A required route parameter or record context was not found (for example client, dog, case, or session id).

docs.title: Save failures
docs.text:
When a save fails:

  1. Check required fields first.
  2. Retry after confirming your session is still active.
  3. If still failing, capture the on-screen error and email support at support@woldsrecord.com.

docs.title: Create a case
docs.text:
From a dog record:

  1. Select Create case.
  2. The app creates a minimal open case and takes you straight to the case edit screen.
  3. Complete or update the intake fields, then save the case.

The edit flow includes core presenting complaint and history/lifestyle context so each case can be completed with structured baseline data.

docs.title: Edit case details
docs.text: Open a case and select Edit to update status, notes, and other intake values as treatment progresses.

docs.title: Case-level navigation
docs.text:
Each case acts as the parent record for sessions and vet reports. Use the case page to:

  • Review current case context
  • Start a new session
  • Open past session entries

docs.title: Dashboard and search
docs.text:
The dashboard and top navigation provide:

  • Global search in the top navigation
  • a Get started checklist for new organisations
  • Upcoming appointments, for organisations with Calendar (beta)
  • a Recent sessions overview
  • the Start a new session launcher

docs.title: Get started checklist
docs.text:
Until you finish setting up, the dashboard shows a Get started card. Each step ticks itself off when you complete it, and the card disappears when every step is done.

The steps you see depend on your role and plan:

Step Shown to Add your practice information, terms and privacy notice Owners and admins Add your first client Everyone except read-only members Add your first dog Everyone except read-only members Preview and share the owner consent form Everyone except read-only members Record your first session Everyone except read-only members Add your practice branding Owners and admins on Pro

To hide the card before you finish, select Hide checklist. This is remembered in the current browser only, so the card shows again in another browser or after you clear your browser data.

docs.title: Search clients and dogs
docs.text:
Use the search control in the top navigation from any signed-in page.

  1. Enter at least 2 characters in the search box.
  2. Review matching clients and dogs.
  3. Select a result to jump directly to that record.

If many results exist, refine your query for a narrower list.

docs.title: Start a new session from the dashboard
docs.text:
Select New Session on the dashboard to open the Start a new session launcher.

  1. In Search client or dog, enter part of the client or dog name.
  2. Select the matching dog and case from the list.
  3. The new session editor opens for that case.

docs.title: Review recent sessions
docs.text:
Use the recent sessions table to quickly navigate to:

  • Client record
  • Dog record
  • Session detail

This is helpful for daily follow-ups and continuity of care.

docs.title: Manage your account
docs.text:
Your account has two pages, both in the Account menu in the header:

  • My Account: your contact details.
  • Personal settings: your appearance and session preferences.

docs.title: My Account
docs.text: Use My Account to keep your contact details current.

docs.title: Update contact details
docs.text:
1. Open the Account menu and select My Account.
  2. Select Edit profile.
  3. Edit your Full name.
  4. Select Save profile.

If successful, you will see Profile updated.

Keep your full name accurate for reports and team visibility.

docs.title: Personal settings
docs.text: Personal settings apply to your account across organisations and devices.

docs.title: Choose light or dark mode
docs.text:
1. Open the Account menu and select Personal settings.
  2. Under Appearance, choose a Colour mode:
    • System: follows your device's light or dark appearance.
    • Light
    • Dark
  3. Select Save personal settings.

docs.title: Choose your default session form
docs.text:
The default session form is the form pre-selected when you create a session. You can still change the form for each session.

  1. Open the Account menu and select Personal settings.
  2. Under Session defaults, choose a Default session form.
  3. Select Save personal settings.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Enable a new practitioner to sign in, create their organisation, and begin recording cases safely.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Sign in using the shared organisation invite email.
  2. Confirm active organisation membership on first load.
  3. Create a client and dog profile.
  4. Open a case and record the presenting complaint.
  5. Capture first session notes and verify save confirmation.

docs.title: Organisation settings
docs.text:
Open Organisation settings to review and maintain core details for your active organisation, including contact and branding-related fields used across the system.

Use Edit details on the Organisation details card to update contact details, the timezone and vet report branding.

docs.title: Beta access
docs.text: Owners and admins can switch beta access on or off from the Beta access card. The change saves straight away and applies to everyone in the organisation. Turning it off asks for confirmation first, because Calendar and public booking links stop working until it is turned back on. Booking data is kept. See Calendar (beta) for full diary and booking guidance.

docs.title: Billing
docs.text:
The Billing card shows your organisation's current plan, billing status and monthly session usage.

Only owners and admins can start or manage subscriptions. Members see the plan details and are asked to contact an owner or admin to change the plan.

docs.title: Plans and upgrades
docs.text:
• Free: includes standard session limits. Owners and admins can select Upgrade to Starter (or Start first month free if eligible) or Choose Pro monthly.
  • Starter: includes unlimited sessions. Owners and admins can switch plan or billing interval, or select Manage billing.
  • Pro: includes unlimited sessions and premium features. Owners and admins can switch plan or billing interval, or select Manage billing.

Subscriptions renew automatically each month or year until cancelled.

docs.title: Change your plan or billing interval
docs.text:
Owners and admins with an active subscription can switch plan, or between monthly and yearly billing, from the Billing card:

  1. Select Switch to next to the plan and interval you want.
  2. Read the price preview. It shows what Stripe will charge now, or credit to your next invoices, for the rest of the billing period.
  3. Select Confirm switch, or Keep current plan to cancel.

The change applies straight away. Switching to yearly or monthly billing moves your renewal date to today. Switching from Pro to Starter stops branded vet reports and organisation export, but your saved logo and records are kept. If the payment fails, your plan stays as it is.

docs.title: Manage or cancel a subscription
docs.text: To update payment details or cancel a subscription, select Manage billing on the Billing card to open the Stripe customer portal. Cancel before your next billing date to avoid renewal.

docs.title: Export organisation data
docs.text: Organisation settings includes export actions.

docs.title: Export formats
docs.text:
• JSON
  • CSV ZIP

docs.title: Export flow
docs.text:
1. Choose your export format.
  2. Start export.
  3. Download begins from a time-limited secure link.

docs.title: Export contents
docs.text:
Exports include:

  • Clients
  • Dogs
  • Cases
  • Sessions

If export cannot start, an error message is shown and you can retry.

docs.title: Create a new session
docs.text:
You can start a new session from a case page or from the dashboard:

  • From a case page: select Create session.
  • From the dashboard or sessions list: select New Session, then search for the client or dog under Search client or dog and choose an open case.

docs.title: Required
docs.text: • Session date/time

docs.title: Common fields available
docs.text:
• Session location
  • Changes since last session
  • New veterinary investigations
  • Guardian concerns
  • Current medication
  • Posture and movement observations
  • Palpation and neurological notes
  • Problem list and clinical impression
  • SMART goals and treatment plan
  • Aftercare and home therapy guidance
  • Follow-up recommended date

docs.title: Session workspace
docs.text: The session editor includes a context rail to keep case/dog/client context visible while writing notes.

docs.title: Save behavior
docs.text: Select Save to save the session. If required fields are missing, inline errors are shown before save completes.

docs.title: Vet practices directory
docs.text: Maintain a reusable list of veterinary contacts for referrals and reports.

docs.title: Add a vet practice
docs.text:
From Vet practices:

  1. Select Add vet practice.
  2. Enter Practice name (required).
  3. Optionally add address, email, phone, vet name, and notes.
  4. Select Create vet practice.

docs.title: Use in workflows
docs.text: Assigned vet practices can be linked to dog records and reused in report workflows.

docs.title: Vet reports
docs.text: Use vet reports to generate practitioner-to-vet summaries from session and case data.

docs.title: Open a vet report
docs.text:
1. Open a session.
  2. Select Vet report.

docs.title: Typical report sections
docs.text:
• Past medical history
  • Current medication
  • Intro / letter context
  • Clinical and treatment summary areas

docs.title: Save and export
docs.text:
• Save report changes before sharing.
  • Use print/export actions to produce a shareable output.
  • If PDF generation is unavailable, browser print is used as fallback.
